html:
The conversion of King Ezana of Aksum to Christianity in the 4th century, around 330. It made Aksum one of the first states to adopt the faith, after Armenia.

The story is told by Roman church historians. A Christian boy from Tyre named Frumentius was shipwrecked on the Red Sea coast and taken to the royal court, where he rose to be a tutor and adviser. Later he travelled to Alexandria and asked its bishop, Athanasius, to send a bishop to Aksum. Athanasius made Frumentius himself the bishop, and he went back to teach.

Ezana's own inscriptions and coins show the change. Early ones honour the old gods and use the crescent and disc. Later ones speak of the God of heaven and the Trinity, and Aksumite coins begin to carry the cross.

Christianity spread slowly from the court to the people, helped by monks from the Roman east. The church stayed tied to Alexandria, which sent its head bishop until the Ethiopian church got its own patriarch in 1959. Aksum also gave shelter to early Muslims in the first Hijra.
sum: The conversion of King Ezana of Aksum to Christianity in the 4th century, around 330. It made Aksum one of the first states to adopt the faith, after Armenia.
